name: Acadia
description: Granite summits, lakes and rocky shoreline on Mount Desert Island and nearby islands in Maine, topped by Cadillac Mountain, the highest point on the US Atlantic coast.

name: American Samoa
description: The only US national park south of the equator spans parts of three Samoan islands, guarding rainforest, volcanic peaks, sandy beaches and coral reefs full of fish.

name: Arches
description: Utah desert park with over 2,000 sandstone arches, Delicate Arch among them, plus balanced rocks, fins and spires shaped by long erosion.

name: Badlands
description: Striped buttes, spires and mixed-grass prairie in southwestern South Dakota, rich in ancient mammal fossils and grazed by bison and bighorn sheep.

name: Big Bend
description: A vast Chihuahuan Desert park where the Rio Grande curves along the Mexican border, with the Chisos Mountains, deep river canyons and many fossils.

name: Biscayne
description: Almost all water, this park covers central Biscayne Bay, mangrove shores, the northern Florida Keys and coral reefs used by manatees and sea turtles.

name: Black Canyon of the Gunnison
fullName: Black Canyon of the Gunnison National Park
description: The Gunnison River has cut a narrow gorge into ancient dark rock here, leaving some of the steepest and deepest canyon walls in North America.

name: Bryce Canyon
description: A series of natural amphitheaters on the edge of the Paunsaugunt Plateau in southern Utah, filled with orange, pink and white rock hoodoos.

name: Canyonlands
description: The Colorado and Green rivers split this Utah park into districts of deep canyons, mesas, buttes and arches, with traces of Ancestral Puebloan life.

name: Capitol Reef
description: Centered on the Waterpocket Fold, a long wrinkle in the crust of south-central Utah that shows colorful rock layers, cliffs, domes and canyons.

name: Carlsbad Caverns
description: More than 100 caves under the Chihuahuan Desert of New Mexico, including the huge Big Room, shelter hundreds of thousands of Mexican free-tailed bats.

name: Channel Islands
description: Five islands off the southern California coast and the sea around them, home to plants and animals found nowhere else, such as the island fox.

name: Chiricahua
description: Hoodoos and stone columns of rhyolite tuff in southeastern Arizona's Chiricahua Mountains, left by a huge eruption about 27 million years ago.

name: Congaree
description: Along the Congaree River in South Carolina, a floodplain with the biggest remaining tract of old-growth bottomland forest in the US and very tall trees.

name: Crater Lake
description: The deepest lake in the US fills the caldera of the collapsed volcano Mount Mazama, famous for its intense blue, clear water and Wizard Island.

name: Cuyahoga Valley
description: Along the Cuyahoga River in Ohio, the valley offers waterfalls, woods, historic buildings, a scenic railroad and the old Ohio and Erie Canal towpath.

name: Death Valley
description: The hottest, driest and lowest national park, straddling California and Nevada, with salt flats at Badwater Basin, sand dunes, canyons and old mines.

name: Denali
description: Huge Alaskan wilderness around Denali, the highest peak in North America, reached by one road and home to grizzly bears, caribou, moose and wolves.

name: Dry Tortugas
description: Small islands at the far western end of the Florida Keys, reached only by boat or plane, with the brick Fort Jefferson, coral reefs and shipwrecks.

name: Everglades
description: The biggest tropical wilderness in the US, a slow river of sawgrass, mangroves and estuaries in south Florida that shelters panthers and manatees.

name: Gates of the Arctic
fullName: Gates of the Arctic National Park and Preserve
description: The northernmost US national park, a roadless area of the Brooks Range in Alaska with no visitor facilities, wild rivers and migrating caribou.

name: Gateway Arch
description: At 91 acres the smallest national park, in St. Louis, it holds the steel arch that honors westward expansion and the Old Courthouse of the Dred Scott case.

name: Glacier
description: Rugged Rocky Mountain peaks, shrinking glaciers and more than 100 lakes in northern Montana, crossed by the Going-to-the-Sun Road.

name: Glacier Bay
fullName: Glacier Bay National Park and Preserve
description: An Alaska bay of fjords and tidewater glaciers that has opened up as the ice retreated since 1794, with whales, seals, bears and mountain goats.

name: Grand Canyon
description: The Colorado River carved this immense canyon in northern Arizona, exposing bands of colored rock that visitors view from both rims.

name: Grand Teton
description: The sharp Teton Range rises abruptly above the sagebrush valley of Jackson Hole and its lakes in northwestern Wyoming.

name: Great Basin
description: Eastern Nevada park around Wheeler Peak, known for bristlecone pines thousands of years old, the limestone Lehman Caves and very dark night skies.

name: Great Sand Dunes
fullName: Great Sand Dunes National Park and Preserve
description: The tallest dunes in North America rise at the base of the Sangre de Cristo Mountains in southern Colorado, next to grasslands, wetlands and forests.

name: Great Smoky Mountains
description: Forested Appalachian ridges on the North Carolina and Tennessee border, rich in plant and animal life, with many trails and old farm buildings.

name: Guadalupe Mountains
description: West Texas park around Guadalupe Peak, the state's highest point, with McKittrick Canyon and the remains of an ancient Permian reef.

name: Haleakalā
description: On Maui, the summit area of the Haleakalā volcano with its vast crater of cinder cones, plus the coastal Kīpahulu area, home to many endangered species.

name: Hawaiʻi Volcanoes
description: On the Island of Hawaiʻi, this park covers Kīlauea and Mauna Loa, two of the most active volcanoes on Earth, from fresh lava fields to rainforest.

name: Hot Springs
description: Thermal springs from the Ouachita Mountains flow through this park in the city of Hot Springs, Arkansas, beside the historic bathhouses of Bathhouse Row.

name: Indiana Dunes
description: Beaches and high sand dunes on Lake Michigan's southern shore, plus prairie, bogs and marshes that support a remarkable variety of species.

name: Isle Royale
description: A remote, roadless island in Lake Superior and hundreds of small islets around it, known for shipwrecks, hiking and its wolves and moose.

name: Joshua Tree
description: Where the Mojave and Colorado deserts meet in southern California, with forests of Joshua trees and giant piles of rounded granite boulders.

name: Katmai
description: On the Alaska Peninsula, a land of volcanoes, including the 1912 Valley of Ten Thousand Smokes, where grizzly bears gather to fish for salmon.

name: Kenai Fjords
description: Near Seward, Alaska, the Harding Icefield feeds many glaciers that flow down to the sea; Exit Glacier is the one part reachable by road.

name: Kings Canyon
description: Next to Sequoia in California's Sierra Nevada, with a deep granite canyon of the Kings River and giant sequoia groves, including the General Grant Tree.

name: Kobuk Valley
description: Arctic park in northwest Alaska on the Kobuk River, with large active sand dunes and a route crossed by huge herds of migrating caribou.

name: Lake Clark
fullName: Lake Clark National Park and Preserve
description: Southwest Alaska park with active volcanoes such as Mount Redoubt, glaciers, rivers, waterfalls, rainforest, tundra and three mountain ranges.

name: Lassen Volcanic
description: Northern California park with all four types of volcano, including Lassen Peak, a lava dome, and boiling mud pots, steam vents and hot pools.

name: Mammoth Cave
description: Beneath the hills of central Kentucky lies the longest known cave system in the world, with cave life above the Green River valley.

name: Mesa Verde
description: Southwest Colorado park with thousands of Ancestral Puebloan sites, including Cliff Palace, built into canyon walls in the 1100s and 1200s.

name: Mount Rainier
description: An ice-clad active volcano in Washington's Cascade Range, wrapped in glaciers and in summer meadows full of wildflowers.

name: New River Gorge
fullName: New River Gorge National Park and Preserve
description: No river gorge in the eastern US is deeper than this West Virginia canyon, crossed by the New River Gorge Bridge and loved by whitewater rafters.

name: North Cascades
description: Jagged, heavily glaciated peaks in northern Washington, with deep valleys and a large backcountry wilderness reached on foot.

name: Olympic
description: On Washington's Olympic Peninsula, the park runs from wild Pacific beaches through temperate rainforests such as the Hoh to glacier-capped peaks.

name: Petrified Forest
description: Northeastern Arizona badlands with large deposits of fossilized wood about 225 million years old, the colorful Painted Desert and ancient rock art.

name: Pinnacles
description: Rock spires in central California, left from part of an old volcano, where rock climbers come and endangered California condors fly free.

name: Redwood
description: Run jointly with state parks in northern California, it protects old-growth coast redwoods, the world's tallest trees, plus prairie and a wild coast.

name: Rocky Mountain
description: High peaks, alpine tundra and lakes on both sides of the Continental Divide in northern Colorado, with elk, moose and Longs Peak.

name: Saguaro
description: Two districts on either side of Tucson, Arizona, protect Sonoran Desert landscapes dense with giant saguaro cacti and other desert life.

name: Sequoia
description: In California's southern Sierra Nevada, the Giant Forest holds the General Sherman Tree, and the park reaches the highest summit in the lower 48 states.

name: Shenandoah
description: A long, narrow park on the Blue Ridge in Virginia, followed by Skyline Drive and the Appalachian Trail through hardwood forest.

name: Theodore Roosevelt
description: Three units of North Dakota badlands that shaped Theodore Roosevelt, with his old cabin, scenic drives, bison, pronghorn and wild horses.

name: Virgin Islands
description: Covers much of the island of St. John, with white beaches, coral reefs, Taíno sites and the ruins of colonial sugar plantations.

name: Voyageurs
description: A lake and forest park on the Minnesota-Canada border, named for French fur traders, best explored by canoe, kayak or boat.

name: White Sands
description: In New Mexico's Tularosa Basin, the largest gypsum dune field on Earth forms a sea of brilliant white sand.

name: Wind Cave
description: A huge cave system, among the longest on the planet, known for rare boxwork formations, under a South Dakota prairie where bison and prairie dogs live.

name: Wrangell–St. Elias
fullName: Wrangell–St. Elias National Park and Preserve
description: The largest US national park, in Alaska, where four mountain ranges meet, with many of North America's highest peaks and vast glaciers.

name: Yellowstone
description: The first national park, mostly in Wyoming, sits on a volcanic caldera with geysers such as Old Faithful, hot springs, a great canyon and bison herds.

name: Yosemite
description: In California's Sierra Nevada, granite cliffs such as El Capitan and Half Dome, tall waterfalls and giant sequoias surround Yosemite Valley.

name: Zion
description: Southwest Utah park of towering sandstone cliffs and narrow canyons cut by the Virgin River, including the Narrows and Angels Landing.
